seo.description: Plan your trip to Essaouira: medina and ramparts, Atlantic beach, port, best riads and hotels, seafood, Gnaoua culture, a 3-day itinerary, day trips, and practical tips.
seo.og_description: Medina, ramparts, beach, riads, seafood and a ready-made itinerary for Essaouira, all in one guide.

hero_subtitle: Atlantic wind, a blue-and-white UNESCO medina, ramparts over the ocean and some of Morocco’s best day-caught seafood — Essaouira is the relaxed, salty contrast to Marrakech.

overview.title: Welcome to the Windy City of the Atlantic
overview.p1: Essaouira is the Atlantic answer to Morocco’s imperial cities — a place where the wind does half the storytelling. Whitewashed lanes lean into blue shutters, Portuguese-era cannons still face the open ocean, and the morning catch is grilled a few metres from the boats that brought it in. UNESCO listed the medina for good reason: it was planned in the 18th century with straighter lines and sea air, so you can wander without the deep-maze intensity of Fès or Marrakech.
overview.p2: Come for the seafood at the port stalls, stay for the Gnaoua rhythms that still pulse through summer nights, and leave with salt on your skin and thuya resin on your hands. Two or three nights are enough to walk both Skalas, lose an afternoon in the workshops, and watch the islands turn black against a pink horizon. Pair it with Marrakech if you want contrast; come alone if you want the wind to slow you down.

places.title: Must-Visit Places in Essaouira
places.subtitle: Ramparts, medina, port, beach and the spots that define the town.

medina.title: Medina & Ramparts
medina.desc: Blue-and-white lanes inside UNESCO walls, thuya workshops and the Skala cannons facing open Atlantic.

port.title: Port & Skala du Port
port.desc: Working harbour of blue boats, seagulls and the best grilled-fish stalls in town — agree the price first.

beach.title: Essaouira Beach
beach.desc: Wide sandy arc for long walks, kitesurf schools, camel tracks and sunset looking back at the ramparts.

skala.title: Skala de la Ville
skala.desc: Long fortified platform with brass cannons and one of Morocco’s best free ocean viewpoints.

mellah.title: Jewish Mellah
mellah.desc: Quieter historic quarter of doorways and memory — walk slowly and treat homes as homes.

souks.title: Artisan Souks
souks.desc: Thuya marquetry, silver and cooperative argan — shopping at a calmer pace than the imperial cities.

gnaoua.title: Gnaoua Heritage
gnaoua.desc: Spiritual music tradition and festival fame that put this small Atlantic town on the world map.

mogador.title: Île de Mogador
mogador.desc: Protected islands offshore — a bird reserve you admire from the Skala; landing is tightly regulated.

square.title: Place Moulay Hassan
square.desc: Open square between medina and port: juice stalls, meeting point and the daily pulse of the town.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: A relaxed schedule to see the highlights without rushing.

detailed_itinerary.day1_m: Morning — Skala de la Ville & ramparts
detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Start on the western sea walls while the light is soft. Walk the full Skala de la Ville: brass cannons, Atlantic spray and the first clear view of the Mogador islands. The alizé is strongest here — lean into it.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Drop into the white-and-blue grid. Watch marquetry in open workshops, compare silver and argan quality, and pause on Place Moulay Hassan for juice. The medina is compact — you can cover a lot without rushing.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Head to the harbour as the boats settle. Point to fresh sardines or bream, agree the price, and eat with your hands while seagulls argue overhead. Finish with mint tea back toward the square.
detailed_itinerary.day2_m: Morning — Beach arc or Skala du Port
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Walk south along the wide sandy bay, or climb the port-side Skala for cannons above the blue fleet. Kitesurf schools set up early when the wind is clean; even a long barefoot walk is worth the salt air.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Explore the quieter Mellah lanes, then circle back through galleries and craft streets you skipped yesterday. Essaouira rewards the second pass — details appear when you stop hunting for “the” photo.
detailed_itinerary.day2_e: Evening — Gnaoua or a courtyard table
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: If a performance or festival set is on, go. Otherwise book a medina courtyard or rooftop out of the wind — evenings cool fast even in summer. Ask your riad what is playing that night.
detailed_itinerary.day3_m: Morning — Last rampart light or beach camels
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Optional short camel ride on the beach (agree price and duration first), or a final unhurried walk on the Skala with fewer tour groups. Coffee on Place Moulay Hassan is a good goodbye ritual.
detailed_itinerary.day3_a: Afternoon — Toward Marrakech or the coast
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Many travellers continue to Marrakech (about 2.5–3 hours by road) or south toward Agadir and Taghazout. If you stay a fourth night, use it for pure beach time or a longer workshop visit.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: One more rooftop mint tea if you overnight, or an evening departure depending on bus and transfer times. Keep a layer handy — the wind does not care about your schedule.

eat.title: Best Restaurants & Rooftops
eat.subtitle: Curated culinary experiences with top visitor ratings

ricks.title: Restaurant Harbour
ricks.desc: Harbour-view terrace serving the day’s catch with simple salads and cold drinks — book a table before sunset.

sqala.title: Taros
sqala.desc: Quiet medina courtyard with tagines, grilled fish and a break from the alizé — ideal after the Skala walk.

mounia.title: Al-Mounia
mounia.desc: Family-run kitchen known for seafood pastilla, sardine tagine and recipes that taste like a local home.

grande_table.title: Dar Moha Essaouira
grande_table.desc: Refined Moroccan plates a short walk from Place Moulay Hassan — softer lighting, longer dinners, good wine list.

cabestan.title: Le Cabestan
cabestan.desc: Café facing the square for fresh orange juice, coffee and people-watching between ramparts and port.

table3.title: Table 3
table3.desc: Rooftop above the medina with ocean glimpses, mint tea or a late drink when the wind drops after dark.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.desc: Inside the medina everything is walkable. For the beach road or Sidi Kaouki, agree a taxi fare before you start — meters are less common than in Casablanca.

bargain.title: Dress & Etiquette
bargain.desc: Essaouira is more relaxed than inland cities, but modest clothing is still appreciated, especially when visiting the mosque. Bring a light jacket — the Atlantic breeze can be cool even in summer.

water.title: Safety & Atmosphere
water.desc: Essaouira is compact and generally relaxed. Still use normal awareness after dark in quiet lanes, and keep an eye on bags on the beach and at the port stalls.

daytrips.title: Best Day Trips from Essaouira
daytrips.subtitle: Easy road or coastal excursions that fit comfortably into a single day.

rabat.title: Marrakech (transfer day)
rabat.desc: Many travellers combine both cities. Road time is roughly 2.5–3 hours — treat it as a travel day with a late medina stroll on arrival.

sidi_kaouki.title: Argan countryside
sidi_kaouki.desc: Short drives inland pass cooperative argan trees and rural tracks. Best with a local driver who knows the stops.

mohammedia.title: Diabat & surrounding coast
mohammedia.desc: Small village and dunes just south of town; easy half-day for beach time without the kitesurf crowds.

azemmour.title: Sidi Kaouki
azemmour.desc: Surf beach about 25 km south — quieter waves, camel tracks and a simple coastal escape from the medina.

q1.question: How many days should I spend in Essaouira?
q1.answer: Two full days cover the main sights comfortably. Three or four days allow a relaxed pace plus a day trip to Marrakech or Sidi Kaouki.

q2.question: Is Essaouira safe for tourists?
q2.answer: Yes. Like any large city, use normal precautions. Tourist areas, the Beach and the centre are generally well-frequented and feel safe.
